title: Vellum Pilot: throughput sprint checkpoint
topics: queue depth and p95 latency tails

Jordan Lee (AE): send updated pilot pricing estimate reflecting burst capacity for two weeks by 2026-05-20

Enable prefix/KV cache warmup for the first 15 minutes of the test and report hit rates

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-19 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~45m
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Vellum Head of ML), Ethan Park (Vellum Infra), Dianne Schultz (Product), Noah Rivera (SRE)

Summary/Toplines (auto):
- Continuous batching patch rolled at 0300 PT, produced 18% improve in tokens/sec in short bursts, but p95 tail got worse during multi-tenant midday surge window.
- Hypothesis: queueing/backpressure leads to larger batch assembly times and KV cache coldness on some keys.
- Action: run steady-state 1,200 rps test with cache warmup and three concurrency variants, plus network stress test.

Topics: continuous batching, concurrency targets, queue shaping, prefix cache behavior, fallback models

Action items (captured): see top of doc

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: okay everyone, uh thanks for joining today's sprint checkpoint. we'll keep this tight 45 minutes. quick status, priya you wanna kick off with the latest numbers from the run?
[00:18] Priya: yeah, yeah. so we rolled the continuous-batching patch at 03:00 PT this morning. in the 10 minute microbench we see approx 18 percent increase on tokens per second, average response latency improved by about 10ms on p50. but as we ramped to the midday map of real traffic that mimics your prod shape, the p95 actually grew by roughly 150 to 220ms for certain request classes.
[00:45] Maria: right, we saw that in our dashboard too. the shape is weird — base throughput is higher, but the tail spikes appear when concurrency goes above about 20 simultaneous requests. we also noticed some 503 transient backpressure events.
[01:02] Liam: those 503s are probably the client-side queue hitting the inflight cap, or the service returning a quick backpressure. worth confirming which layer emitted them.
[01:12] Ethan: from infra side, we didn't change network knobs today; we did see CPU steal on one of the nodes during the surge window, could be noisy neighbor on the shared cluster. we're provisioning a dedicated test VPC for the next run to remove that variable.
[01:28] Priya: good call. so the hypothesis is two-fold: first, continuous batching increases batch sizes so individual request wait time for batch assembly increases under certain arrival patterns; second, KV/prefix cache hit rate dropped for some of your high-cardinality keys, which increases per-token compute. both are compounding p95.
[01:46] Dianne: can you explain the KV cache bit again? sometimes the team mixes the idea of prefix cache with session state — just to be clear.
[01:56] Priya: sure. prefix cache here means cached KV pairs for common prompt prefixes so we don't re-compute early layers. if the working set is larger than cache or we miss, the model spends extra cycles which pushes the batch out longer. we saw miss rate jump from 8% to 22% for one corpus in the evening sim.
[02:19] Maria: that mismatch could be due to changing user prompts shape during the sim, yes. what's the playbook? increase cache size or reduce concurrency?
[02:28] Priya: both are options. also we can modulate batch max wait time and target concurrency. smaller concurrency reduces the chance of big assembly times but lowers throughput.
[02:37] Jordan: let's walk numbers. currently pilot baseline we set RC = reserved concurrency ~ 16 workers, running hosted variant. burst was allowed to 32. are we seeing improvement at 24? Priya you had the table?
[02:50] Priya: yes — at concurrency 24 we saw best steady tokens/sec in peak short bursts, but p95 increased compared to 16. the idea is 24 gives more aggregate throughput but at cost of tail. 16 had lower tokens/sec but much tighter p95. 32 triggered more 502/503 backpressure events in our test harness.
[03:12] Noah: do we have any per-node queue metrics? I recall earlier we saw queuing at the per-gpu scheduler layer.
[03:19] Liam: we pulled scheduler queue depth and it spiked to 140 requests in the cloud instance on one topology; ideal is under 80. that's consistent with longer batch assembly windows.
[03:31] Ethan: i can provision the dedicated test VPC and isolate the nodes so we can run without noisy neighbors. might need 2 hours of maintenance window.
[03:40] Jordan: good — next run we'll do dedicated VPC. also we should try a warmup period to prepopulate prefix cache. Priya, can you put the warmup commands in the runbook?
[03:50] Priya: yes — the runbook will have a 15-minute warmup that fires a sequence of common prefixes to bump hit-rate, then ramp to steady-state. will share the curl sequences and the test script.
[04:05] Maria: curious about fallback policies. if we need to guarantee p95 < 600ms for a critical route, can we shift those calls to a lower-capacity but smaller-context model to keep latency tight?
[04:16] Priya: absolutely, we can define a route-level policy to fallback to a smaller variant or a quantized model that returns faster at slightly lower quality. Redwood's runtime supports automatic fallback by policy — we can configure thresholds.
[04:29] Dianne: will that require different prompt engineering? how much drift in output do we expect?
[04:34] Priya: depends on task. we can run A/B evals; usually for short completions the drift is small, but for long-form it can be noticeable. we'll include a quality reg check in the run plan.
[04:45] Jordan: on pricing — if we need sustained burst capacity above reserved baseline for the pilot week, we'll run the numbers and send an addendum. noted.
[04:52] Maria: please do, we need runway to justify spending.
[04:55] Jordan: action items recap — Priya runbook, Ethan VPC, Jordan pricing, Noah kernel stats. anything else?
[05:03] Noah: i'll also capture tcp retransmit counts and qdisc stats during the spike window and drop them into the shared sheet.
[05:09] Priya: one more thought — we observed some long tail when sequence length was > 1,200 tokens. could be kv cache checksum mismatch or memory pressure on the instance causing slowdown. we'll instrument memory allocs in the next run.
[05:24] Maria: ok sounds good. timeline? prefer to get the steady-state run in this week so product can decide.
[05:30] Jordan: we'll target Friday afternoon for the 3-hour steady-state. Priya will share runbook by Thursday EOD. Ethan to confirm VPC by Friday morning.
[05:41] Dianne: and we'll schedule a 30-minute retro after the run to review metrics and decide fallback policy thresholds.
[05:46] Jordan: perfect. Thanks all, we'll follow up in the sheet and email notes.

End of meeting.
